name: Familial Progressive Hyperpigmentation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Progressive Hyperpigmentation

criteria.description: Presence of progressive, diffuse, and patchy hyperpigmented macules and patches appearing in infancy or early childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing increased melanin deposition in basal keratinocytes without melanocyte proliferation
No evidence of systemic disease or internal organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive hyperpigmentation with positive family history and supportive histopathology findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing may be inconclusive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive diffuse hyperpigmented macules and patches
pathognomonic.notes: Typically appears in infancy or early childhood and progresses over time
searchTerms: progressive dark spots over large areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Zosteriform or cribriform pattern of hyperpigmentation
searchTerms: skin darkening in band or net pattern

common.symptomName: Hyperpigmentation involving face, trunk, and extremities
searchTerms: dark skin patches on face, body, limbs

common.symptomName: Absence of preceding inflammation or erythema
common.notes: Pigmentation develops without inflammatory skin changes
searchTerms: no redness or swelling before pigmentation
absence of skin irritation before spots

common.symptomName: Persistence and gradual progression of pigmentation over years
searchTerms: slowly increasing dark spots over years

common.symptomName: Normal hair, nails, and mucous membranes
searchTerms: normal hair, nails, and mouth lining
no abnormalities in hair or nails

occasional.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to hyperpigmented areas
searchTerms: mild itching limited to pigmented areas

occasional.symptomName: Slight textural changes of affected skin
occasional.notes: Rarely, slight thickening or roughness noted

occasional.symptomName: Mild cosmetic concern or psychological distress

searchTerms: slight excess hair on dark patches
mild hair growth over pigmented areas
temporary mild redness before dark spots

other: Skin biopsy showing increased melanin in basal keratinocytes without melanocyte proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Unilateral blue-gray pigmentation localized to periorbital area
No progressive spread beyond initial area
Photosensitivity and early onset skin cancers

redFlags: Rapid onset of pigmentation with systemic symptoms
Signs of adrenal insufficiency or endocrine dysfunction
